title: Correlation between PSLE Results and Socio-economic Status in Past Two Years
what_it_is: Correlation between PSLE Results and Socio-economic Status in Past Two Years

sections.label: Socio-economic background and PSLE results
sections.summary: In Singapore, there is some correlation between socio-economic background and PSLE results.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In Singapore, there is similarly some correlation between socio-economic background and PSLE results.

sections.label: MOE support for higher-needs students
sections.summary: MOE pays close attention to this issue and provides significantly more support to students with higher needs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: MOE pays close attention to this issue and provides significantly more support to students with higher needs.

sections.label: UPLIFT and support for students in need
sections.summary: UPLIFT was launched to enhance upstream wraparound support for students with needs beyond academic support, and schools with more students in need receive more manpower and funds.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Some students also have needs that extend beyond academic support.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: This is why we have launched the Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce (UPLIFT), which I currently chair, to enhance our upstream wraparound support for such students.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Schools with a higher proportion of students in need also receive more manpower and funds to support whole-school interventions for their students.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Education (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: OECD’s PISA study, for example, has found that compared to other high-performing systems, Singapore’s students from the bottom-25% of socio-economic background not only outperform their international counterparts of similar socio-economic background, but also out-perform the OECD average in all core domains assessed in PISA.

sections.label: Correlation stability and UPLIFT outcomes
sections.summary: The correlation has been stable over the last five years, and UPLIFT, started in 2018, has had encouraging initial outcomes that are being tracked and monitored.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: On the correlation, it has been stable over the last five years – it has not been going up, not going down.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: On the outcomes of UPLIFT, I hope Mr Ng will give us some time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We just started in 2018 and the initial outcomes have been quite encouraging.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: We are tracking and monitoring different components of the programme.
